items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: And of course the guitarist, Charlie Dixon, from over in New Jersey was another guy that picked up arranging and turned out to be terrific.

ctx.x: Don Redmon, who was one of the greatest arrangers, in my estimation, and one of the greatest rehearsers of a band --

he was Fletcher's first alto saxophonist and arranger, one of the very first ones with Fletcher. Even before Fletcher had started to really get out into the arranging field, Don first started Fletcher's book -- Don Redmond. And of course the guitarist, Charlie Dixon, from over in New Jersey was another guy that picked up arranging and turned out to be terrific.

But getting back to Don -- Don made a few of these sessions. It got so interesting they'd talk about it on the bandstand. Don'd say, 'Why don't you guys invite me up some time?' Hawk said, 'Sure.' He'd come up and Don would bring his horn, and they'd talk, and of course Don knew all that stuff, and he would help out with these guys. And I've got some old records of Fletcher's, and this is why -- I think you didn't hear too many (unintelligible) blues.
